testResults.name: bicep-build-and-lint
testResults.result: The Key Vault-backed Container Apps composition compiled and linted without diagnostics

testResults.name: azure-resource-group-validation
testResults.command: az deployment group validate --resource-group fca-rg-westus2 --parameters infra/parameters/dev.local.bicepparam
testResults.result: Azure validation succeeded without deploying the unseeded references

testResults.name: runtime-vault-access
testResults.result: The runtime managed identity has Key Vault Secrets User scoped only to fca-ml-dev-kv-obj3kww, and both workloads already use that identity

testResults.name: secret-reference-contract
testResults.result: API references alpaca-api-key, alpaca-api-secret, and api-bearer-token through versionless Key Vault URLs; ingest references only the two Alpaca secrets. Environment variables use secretRef and no secret value is a Bicep parameter or tracked setting

testResults.name: authorized-secret-seeding
testResults.result: The signed-in maintainer has Key Vault Administrator on the vault. The two Alpaca credentials are present, and api-bearer-token is generated as an application-owned random token without exposing its value

testResults.name: deployed-secret-references
testResults.result: The three enabled Key Vault names are ready; deployment remains pending until the T140 commit is pushed

testResults.name: controlled-provider-and-ingest-verification
testResults.result: A bounded Azure-hosted Alpaca request and persistence check requires the seeded credentials and deployed references

blockers: The T140 commit must be pushed and the hosted deployment must prove the three Key Vault references resolve. Secret values must not be sent through chat or stored in task evidence.
